sources.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health - TechCrunch
passages: Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features.
Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health.
But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.
“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding.
Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled.
The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users.
It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet.
Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models.
The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.
Ivan covers global consumer tech developments at TechCrunch.

Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys. Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues. Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.” The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week . sources.title: Apple's New Research App Is Designed To Make AI Health Tools More User-Friendly - Engadget
passages: Apple has unveiled a new research study with the aim of learning how people use AI health tools in order to make them more effective and user-friendly.

The company is launching the Health AI Usage Study in conjunction with OpenEvidence , a clinical AI platform used by health professionals that draws medical data from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine .
Participants will use the app to ask medical questions via text-based prompts like "how can I improve my heart health," according to the app's screen shots.
They'll then receive non-jargony responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources.
A key part of the research is a new app now available for download , with Apple aiming to have up to 200,000 participants.
Users must live in the US and be 21 or older, and have an iPhone 15 Pro or later model running iOS 26 and up.
They can choose to share (or not) Apple HealthKit data, including activity levels, sleep quality and lab results, for extra context around their health.
Apple notes that the app is not integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence, and said that participant data will remain confidential and won't be used to train AI models.
"[We] believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding," said Apple VP of Health and fitness Sumbul Desai, MD, in a statement.

"Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey."

sources.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
passages: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.

Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” said Sumbul Desai, MD, Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness.
The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.

The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine.
The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute.
But privacy is a priority, and Apple says it has taken measures to ensure users’ information remains confidential and the data collected won’t be used to train AI models.
Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources.
Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life.

Most users said they wanted information right away, but some also said they were turning to AI because they don’t have a doctor or other provider.
Four out of five doctors are using AI in their practice, up from 38% in 2023, according to an American Medical Association survey earlier this year.

Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health.

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding.
Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled.

extraction.body: Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys. Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues. Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.” The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week . sources.title: Amazon's Zoox partners with Uber to reach more robotaxi riders — first in Las Vegas, then LA - CNBC
passages: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.

sources.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
passages: Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.
The company’s robotaxis only cover heavy tourist zones, like the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District.

sources.title: Zoox robotaxis are now on the Uber app in Las Vegas
passages: Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.
Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride.
Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies.
Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028.
Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.

coreStoryFacts.text: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.
Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.
The company’s robotaxis only cover heavy tourist zones, like the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District.

Nearly a year later, in August 2026, it moved to paid trips.

Riders get two front doors to the same vehicle.

extraction.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs. A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces. A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.
Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X.
"The American people deserve answers," he added.

Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China.
A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.
Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.
US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.
The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.
Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.
Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.
Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.
Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.
Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.
An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs.
A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces.
A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

extraction.body: Members of Congress are calling on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign, and momentum is building to subpoena the executive, whose company is a leader in advanced artificial intelligence chips. Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China. Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy . The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk. "What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18. GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter . Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it. Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond. Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes." Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this." "We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said. The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May. "Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs. "I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate." Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down. "From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good." Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill. Democrats are widely expected to launch myriad investigations into the White House and industry when they assume control of both chambers of Congress in January. Nvidia is now likely to be at the center of those probes. "There's two parts to this investigation that [need] to happen somewhere immediately," Subramanyam said. "One is what was going on with Nvidia and China, and two is why the administration did nothing about it even though they appeared to have known, and what the administration knew, and what influence the money from Nvidia and Jensen Huang had on this administration, essentially staying silent." Rep. Jay Obernolte , R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, said Tuesday he hopes that the Huang scandal can avoid becoming a distraction in talks about imposing export controls on advanced AI chips. The situation may give Congress additional ammunition as it tries to pass a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips. Congress has still not passed the annual defense bill, which is a top priority for lawmakers in the lame-duck session. Those bills include the AI Overwatch Act , the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act — all of which are aimed at preventing U.S. chip technology from falling into adversarial hands. Sens. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., in a statement following the revelation of Huang's affair, urged their colleagues to include the AI Overwatch Act. Warren, the incoming Senate banking committee chair, sponsored the bill in the Senate with Banks. "Huang's confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China's intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer about the extent to which these activities were related," the senators said. "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips." And Subramanyam warned that what Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could affect its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down. "If Nvidia finds out that he knew about what was going on and does nothing about it, then Nvidia is making a choice and us as regulators and as watchdogs need to defend the American people," he said. extraction.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs. A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces. A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs.
A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces.
A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China. Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy . The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk. "What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18. GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter . Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it. Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond. Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes." Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this." "We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said. The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May. "Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs. "I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate." Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down. "From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good." Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill. Democrats are widely expected to launch myriad investigations into the White House and industry when they assume control of both chambers of Congress in January. Nvidia is now likely to be at the center of those probes. "There's two parts to this investigation that [need] to happen somewhere immediately," Subramanyam said. "One is what was going on with Nvidia and China, and two is why the administration did nothing about it even though they appeared to have known, and what the administration knew, and what influence the money from Nvidia and Jensen Huang had on this administration, essentially staying silent." Rep. Jay Obernolte , R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, said Tuesday he hopes that the Huang scandal can avoid becoming a distraction in talks about imposing export controls on advanced AI chips. The situation may give Congress additional ammunition as it tries to pass a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips. Congress has still not passed the annual defense bill, which is a top priority for lawmakers in the lame-duck session. Those bills include the AI Overwatch Act , the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act — all of which are aimed at preventing U.S. chip technology from falling into adversarial hands. Sens. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., in a statement following the revelation of Huang's affair, urged their colleagues to include the AI Overwatch Act. Warren, the incoming Senate banking committee chair, sponsored the bill in the Senate with Banks. "Huang's confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China's intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer about the extent to which these activities were related," the senators said. "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips." And Subramanyam warned that what Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could affect its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down. "If Nvidia finds out that he knew about what was going on and does nothing about it, then Nvidia is making a choice and us as regulators and as watchdogs need to defend the American people," he said. passages: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.

sources.title: Zoox robotaxis are now on the Uber app in Las Vegas - TechCrunch
passages: Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.
Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride.
Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028.
Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies.
Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.

The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies. Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East. Uber has partnered with more than 30 companies developing autonomous vehicle technology for sidewalk delivery robots, self-driving cars, robotaxis, and drones — though not all of those have turned into commercial deployments yet. For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo. The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas. Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027. Rides will be available via the Uber app next year as well. For now, all eyes are on Las Vegas, Zoox’s first commercial market and a city where Uber has ambitious robotaxi plans. The two companies also announced a multi-year partnership with MGM Resorts International: they’re rideshare and robotaxi partners for MGM Resorts properties in Las Vegas. Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis. Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox. Zoox’s addition to the Uber app comes with some initial limitations. Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially. Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride. Customers can increase their chances of getting a Zoox robotaxi by opting for autonomous rides through “ride preferences” in the Uber app’s settings. Uber plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in its app as “availability and reliability improve,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call in November. “Las Vegas will become the first U.S. city where riders can access two fully driverless partners through the Uber app,” he said on the call. “We will begin with limited fleets and expand supply over the coming months, with plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in our app.” The plan to offer a dedicated autonomous option marks a shift in Uber’s approach to robotaxis, including its partnership with Waymo. That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028. Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities. TechCrunch previously confirmed with Uber that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. And unlike its partnership with other AV developers, Uber told TechCrunch that it will not provide maintenance and other services for Zoox in the Las Vegas market. passages: Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.

coreStoryFacts.text: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.
Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.

story.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber

facts.text: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.
Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.
Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride.
Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028.
Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies.
Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.
Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.
Uber riders in Las Vegas can now be matched with a robotaxi that has no steering wheel, no pedals and no front seat.
The vehicle comes from Zoox, the autonomous driving company owned by Amazon .
Las Vegas is already a crowded robotaxi market.
Multiple operators, Waymo included, offer autonomous rides in the city.
Uber adding Zoox gives its riders access to one more option without leaving the app they already use.
Nearly a year later, in August 2026, it moved to paid trips.
US vehicle safety rules were written assuming a human driver sits behind a wheel.
Roughly 62 Zoox vehicles were reported in operation across Las Vegas and the Bay Area as of mid-November 2026.
The integration breaks new ground for each company.
It is the first time Uber has put a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle on its network.
Uber and Zoox announced their partnership on March 11, 2026.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi highlighted the importance of the tie-up during the company’s third-quarter earnings call.
The Zoox deal lands while Uber’s arrangement with Waymo is being reshaped.
Waymo plans to end its exclusive routing partnership with Uber in certain markets by January 2028.
Zoox has also pushed its service area into the Arts District and downtown Las Vegas.
Zoox will keep running its own dedicated app alongside the Uber integration.
Riders get two front doors to the same vehicle.

sources.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
passages: Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.

The vehicle comes from Zoox, the autonomous driving company owned by Amazon .
Las Vegas is already a crowded robotaxi market.

Uber adding Zoox gives its riders access to one more option without leaving the app they already use.
Nearly a year later, in August 2026, it moved to paid trips.
US vehicle safety rules were written assuming a human driver sits behind a wheel.

The integration breaks new ground for each company.

Uber and Zoox announced their partnership on March 11, 2026.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi highlighted the importance of the tie-up during the company’s third-quarter earnings call.
The Zoox deal lands while Uber’s arrangement with Waymo is being reshaped.
Waymo plans to end its exclusive routing partnership with Uber in certain markets by January 2028.
Zoox has also pushed its service area into the Arts District and downtown Las Vegas.
Zoox will keep running its own dedicated app alongside the Uber integration.
Riders get two front doors to the same vehicle.

Most robotaxis on US roads today are regular cars retrofitted with sensors and software. Zoox took a different route. Its vehicle was designed from scratch for autonomous driving. The robotaxi seats four passengers who face each other. There is no steering wheel and no pedals, and the vehicle is bidirectional, meaning it can travel either way without needing to turn around. US vehicle safety rules were written assuming a human driver sits behind a wheel. Zoox’s vehicle became the first purpose-built autonomous vehicle approved for paid rides in the US, via an exemption from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). passages: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company's recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders.
Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Nvidia's stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang's departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding .

The petition states that its signers are "concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process" and demands that the board "bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts." It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public.

After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice, they said.A signatory who describes himself as an engineer at Nvidia called Huang an essential part of the company in a comment on the website. His private affairs are none of my business, and if his actions violated our code of conduct, it has to be dealt with. Please bring him back and give him fair treatment, taking his track record and importance for NVIDIA and the wider community into account, the employee told Business Insider.135859064Bring Jensen back petitionHere's what Bring Jensen Huang back petition reads:We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests.For thirty-three years, Jensen poured his heart and soul into building NVIDIA. Many of us stayed because of how he treated the work: as something worth getting right, together, at whatever hour it took. It deserves fairness now.Our understanding is that an outside investigation has been announced but has not yet concluded. We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process. We do not have access to the Board’s private deliberations. Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen's leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.We ask the Board to take three actions:Reinstate Jensen as CEO. Bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.Ensure an independent investigation and a fair hearing. Disclose the inquiry’s scope, independence, and expected timeline, and give Jensen a meaningful opportunity to respond before reaching a final decision.Provide a timely public explanation. Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice.Thank you, Jensen. Elon Musk and Replit CEO Amjad Masad are among those who has signed the petition with organizers claiming more than 100,000 signatures. Stand with Jensen is the online petition asking Nvidia's board of directors to bring Jensen Huang back to the helm of the company after his November 12 resignation. A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too, the Tesla and SpaceX CEO wrote on X. The Stand with Jensen petition also garnered signatures from big names such as Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.ALSO READ: Airplane crash at Miami airportPetition to reinstate Jensen Huang gets tractionA website for the campaign, dubbed Stand with Jensen, said the list includes more than 58,000 shareholders, more than 5,600 current Nvidia employees, and over 1,000 former employees. In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were actively working to remove fake signatures.One Nvidia employee who signed the letter told Business Insider that similar efforts are happening inside the company. A post with similar sentiments appeared on an internal portal where employees can submit questions and suggestions, they said.ALSO READ: Why is Denny’s restoring Jensen Huang’s plaque after removing it?According to a report in The Wired, post had garnered 1,600 comments as of Thursday — a figure that has now more than doubled, the employee said.The Stand with Jensen organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and meaningful due process. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice, they said.A signatory who describes himself as an engineer at Nvidia called Huang an essential part of the company in a comment on the website. His private affairs are none of my business, and if his actions violated our code of conduct, it has to be dealt with. Please bring him back and give him fair treatment, taking his track record and importance for NVIDIA and the wider community into account, the employee told Business Insider.135859064Bring Jensen back petitionHere's what Bring Jensen Huang back petition reads:We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests.For thirty-three years, Jensen poured his heart and soul into building NVIDIA. Many of us stayed because of how he treated the work: as something worth getting right, together, at whatever hour it took. It deserves fairness now.Our understanding is that an outside investigation has been announced but has not yet concluded. We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process. We do not have access to the Board’s private deliberations. Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen's leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.We ask the Board to take three actions:Reinstate Jensen as CEO. Bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.Ensure an independent investigation and a fair hearing. Disclose the inquiry’s scope, independence, and expected timeline, and give Jensen a meaningful opportunity to respond before reaching a final decision.Provide a timely public explanation. Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice.Thank you, Jensen. We stand with you.Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEOEarlier this week, Nvidia's board of directors announced an investigation into whether Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort after he admitted to having an affair in a letter to employees. Days later, Huang resigned following reports of another affair with an Nvidia executive. The board appointed Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor.An October report by The New York Times said Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based tech executive at Megaspeed. On Thursday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice had not reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang was a spy.
