extraction.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs. A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces. A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China. Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy . The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk. "What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18. GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter . Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it. Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond. Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes." Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this." "We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said. The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May. "Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs. "I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate." Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down. "From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good." Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill. Democrats are widely expected to launch myriad investigations into the White House and industry when they assume control of both chambers of Congress in January. Nvidia is now likely to be at the center of those probes. "There's two parts to this investigation that [need] to happen somewhere immediately," Subramanyam said. "One is what was going on with Nvidia and China, and two is why the administration did nothing about it even though they appeared to have known, and what the administration knew, and what influence the money from Nvidia and Jensen Huang had on this administration, essentially staying silent." Rep. Jay Obernolte , R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, said Tuesday he hopes that the Huang scandal can avoid becoming a distraction in talks about imposing export controls on advanced AI chips. The situation may give Congress additional ammunition as it tries to pass a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips. Congress has still not passed the annual defense bill, which is a top priority for lawmakers in the lame-duck session. Those bills include the AI Overwatch Act , the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act — all of which are aimed at preventing U.S. chip technology from falling into adversarial hands. Sens. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., in a statement following the revelation of Huang's affair, urged their colleagues to include the AI Overwatch Act. Warren, the incoming Senate banking committee chair, sponsored the bill in the Senate with Banks. "Huang's confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China's intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer about the extent to which these activities were related," the senators said. "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips." And Subramanyam warned that what Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could affect its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down. "If Nvidia finds out that he knew about what was going on and does nothing about it, then Nvidia is making a choice and us as regulators and as watchdogs need to defend the American people," he said. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. An AI tool is set to be used to replace 22 social care jobs. A new survey is launched to learn how to best prepare students for future workplaces. passages: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.

The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.
Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride.
Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028.
Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies.
Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.

Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.

coreStoryFacts.text: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.
Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.

sources.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
passages: Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too.

For Uber, the company doesn’t build its own self-driving cars. It wants to be the place where everyone else’s self-driving cars find customers.
By opening its fleet to a third-party app for the first time, Zoox gains instant access to Uber’s existing rider base in Las Vegas.
A fleet of about 62 vehicles split between two regions means most Uber trips in Las Vegas will still be handled by human drivers. The pairing is a possibility, not a promise.
Zoox’s paid service depends on its NHTSA exemption. Any change in how federal regulators treat vehicles without manual controls would directly affect how far this model can scale.
The Grand Prix deal starting in 2027 will be a visible stress test. Major events bring crowds, road closures and heavy demand.

story.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber

facts.text: Amazon 's Zoox is making its toaster-shaped self-driving vehicles available through the Uber app in Las Vegas starting this summer, the latest sign of momentum in the nascent but fast-growing robotaxi market.
"This partnership is an opportunity to continue advancing the use of autonomous mobility in daily life," Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said in a statement.
"Through our collaboration, Zoox will provide a differentiated rider experience to those who already know and love the convenience of riding with Uber."
Amazon, which acquired Zoox in 2020, is way behind Alphabet's Waymo, the U.S. robotaxi leader.
Waymo said in February that it had surpassed 400,000 weekly rides across six U.S. metro areas.
It's now operating its service commercially in 10 U.S. cities, and aiming for expansion to London and Tokyo in 2026.
Zoox began offering free driverless rides last year around the Las Vegas Strip and certain San Francisco neighborhoods.
While it's served more than 300,000 riders, the company said in early March it's not yet offering paid rides.
Earlier this week, Zoox announced an expansion of its testing efforts across some cities in the South.

During Uber's fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts that AVs available via his company's app attain "significantly higher utilization" than robotaxis hailed on "stand-alone platforms," basing those estimates on unspecified publicly available data.
Trips per AV, per day are 30% higher on Uber, Khosrowshahi said.
As first-party robotaxi brand services and apps become more familiar to travelers and commuters, they could take market share away from Uber and rivals like Lyft or DiDi in China.
Zoox is seeking an exemption from U.S. regulators to commercially deploy its robotaxis.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday opened up public comments on Zoox's petition, which seeks permission to operate up to 2,500 vehicles on U.S. roads.
As part of a multiyear partnership announced Wednesday, the companies said they plan to make Zoox rides available in Los Angeles next year.
In both cities, Zoox will continue to offer rides on its own app as well.
The Zoox robotaxis have been nicknamed "toasters" due to their shape, with a low step, doors that automatically open and close, and seats that face each other.
Regulators previously gave approval for Zoox to deploy its custom-built vehicles for research and demonstration purposes only.
For Uber, the alliance comes as executives pitch the company's platform as the best way for autonomous vehicle makers to tap rider demand.
Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas.

Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027.

Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially.
Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride.
Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028.
Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies.
Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.
Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon.
Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app.
Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge.

MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations.
Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding.

Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.

The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders.
Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.

Nvidia's stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang's departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding .

It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public.

Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia has triggered a political fight over how closely he worked with President Donald Trump and how much access the United States should allow for advanced artificial intelligence chips to reach China. Huang “met with Trump on multiple occasions, traveled with him to the United Kingdom, and in May accompanied him on Air Force One during his visit to China,” placing his role at the center of Washington’s export-control debate. Washington’s export restrictions since 2022 have been described as difficult to enforce because customers can buy chips in countries like Singapore and Malaysia and then ship them to China.
Aşiatic cloud providers use third-party routes to preserve Nvidia access

The Washington Post framed the controversy as a “shadow war for Trump’s ear on China,” describing how Huang “secured his blessing to sell artificial intelligence chips to China” and fueled backlash among “national security hawks.” The dispute has expanded from chip sales to questions about what the U.S. government knew and what it did, after the BBC reported allegations that a supposed romantic relationship involved “Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company.”
U.S. intelligence suspicions have focused on Alice Huang, and the BBC reported that “U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang has ties to Chinese intelligence,” while Beijing rejects the allegations.
Nvidia’s board has denied any compromise, and the BBC said “there is no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.”

The BBC described the export-control responsibility of U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick and said his department was “pressured to act on concerns about Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.”
Lutnick “received a highly classified memorandum” and “resisted taking action against the company,” a decision now under scrutiny.
The Washington Post said Rubio’s intervention “helped topple” a corporate voice on China, and it tied that shift to momentum for “tougher restrictions” on advanced technology reaching Beijing.

House members from both parties have demanded answers about how the Commerce Department evaluated Chinese companies allowed to buy AI chips, and the BBC said Democrats launched an inquiry into that evaluation. The BBC reported that Republicans also questioned the government’s approach and that pressure is mounting politically as House members demand explanations. Jensen Huang’s team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he “plans to cooperate with their request to testify in a closed session,” keeping the dispute focused on what was known inside government.

A continuing gap in export controls has been described, with Senator Elizabeth Warren saying Huang’s resignation does not absolve him and urging Lutnick to explain why there are still gaps in export controls. The Washington Post linked the controversy to the administration’s China policy direction, describing how Huang’s access and “blessing” for chip sales to China became a flashpoint for officials pushing to keep powerful technology out of Beijing’s hands.

In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were actively working to remove fake signatures.One Nvidia employee who signed the letter told Business Insider that similar efforts are happening inside the company. A post with similar sentiments appeared on an internal portal where employees can submit questions and suggestions, they said.ALSO READ: Why is Denny’s restoring Jensen Huang’s plaque after removing it?According to a report in The Wired, post had garnered 1,600 comments as of Thursday — a figure that has now more than doubled, the employee said.The Stand with Jensen organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and meaningful due process. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice, they said.A signatory who describes himself as an engineer at Nvidia called Huang an essential part of the company in a comment on the website. His private affairs are none of my business, and if his actions violated our code of conduct, it has to be dealt with. Please bring him back and give him fair treatment, taking his track record and importance for NVIDIA and the wider community into account, the employee told Business Insider.135859064Bring Jensen back petitionHere's what Bring Jensen Huang back petition reads:We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests.For thirty-three years, Jensen poured his heart and soul into building NVIDIA. Many of us stayed because of how he treated the work: as something worth getting right, together, at whatever hour it took. It deserves fairness now.Our understanding is that an outside investigation has been announced but has not yet concluded. We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process. We do not have access to the Board’s private deliberations. Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen's leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.We ask the Board to take three actions:Reinstate Jensen as CEO. Bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.Ensure an independent investigation and a fair hearing. Disclose the inquiry’s scope, independence, and expected timeline, and give Jensen a meaningful opportunity to respond before reaching a final decision.Provide a timely public explanation. Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice.Thank you, Jensen. extraction.body: Just three days after the high-profile resignation of the founder of the world's most valuable chipmaker, his supporters in Silicon Valley have set up a dedicated war room to pressure the board of directors. However, regaining the seat will not be easy for the billionaire: he does not hold a controlling stake, while the corporation is already scouting for his replacement and bracing for scrutiny from Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Thursday, November 12, following the exposure of extramarital relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct subordinate, is already discussing a plan to return to the company with his confidants. This was reported on Sunday, November 15, by the British newspaper Financial Times. According to an associate of the businessman, Silicon Valley top executives have formed a dedicated "war room" to lobby Nvidia's board of directors for Huang's reinstatement, as well as to try to secure support in the White House. "Everyone who matters in tech outside of the frontier labs loves Jensen," said an interlocutor of the publication, adding that these efforts have the backing of the former CEO himself. Over the weekend, the public campaign for the return of the founder of the $4 trillion corporation gained momentum. An open letter to the board of directors demanding to "Bring Jensen Back" was supported by Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, as well as several Nvidia employees. Back on Friday, major shareholders of the company—Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management head Gavin Baker—published an appeal to the corporate leadership, urging them to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," given his decades of service and the uncertainty surrounding the future of the business. Despite pressure from billionaires and investors, the push to rehabilitate Huang faces severe legal and political obstacles. Unlike many other tech titan founders, Huang does not hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and therefore cannot veto decisions made by the board of directors. The board itself is currently conducting an independent investigation into the former chief's conduct. Even those in the businessman's camp acknowledge the weakness of his position. "An affair with a subordinate is a firing offense," admitted one member of Huang's support group. Aside from the internal workplace affair with Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, Huang's primary problem stems from his connection to Alice Huang, head of the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which US authorities suspect of espionage and smuggling chips into China. This episode has drawn intense scrutiny toward how Nvidia monitors the sales of its artificial intelligence processors to clients in Asia. On Sunday, November 15, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly called for a "radical refresh" in Nvidia's leadership following the departure of its founder. Meanwhile, the corporation's interim CEO Colette Kress is preparing the company for the release of its quarterly financial report on Tuesday, while the board of directors is already looking for a permanent successor. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia representatives have approached Rene Haas, CEO of the British processor architecture designer Arm Holdings, with an offer to head the corporation, though officially the company states that a formal process to select a new leader has not yet been launched. Representatives of Nvidia and Jensen Huang himself declined to comment on his potential return.

U.S. intelligence was reported to believe that the woman involved in an affair with Jensen Huang, Alice Huang (no relation), is a spy working for the Chinese Ministry of State Security , or MSS.
Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, an AI company accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via a subsidiary called Speedmatrix.
That alone would potentially constitute a violation of Nvidia's own code of conduct.

Just days after he left the company under a cloud of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang might be on his way back to the company he founded.
That's after a number of his allies rallied in support for Huang, including influential SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and outspoken Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

"Huang has discussed with confidantes the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter," the report claimed, adding that allies were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley figures to try and lobby for his return.

Now, an open letter sent to Nvidia's board by Huang's allies has urged them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.” The open letter was penned by Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker, both shareholders.

Huang has only admitted to the affair with the alleged spy, Alice Huang, whom he is not related to. Despite the seriousness and recency of the philandering accusations, Huang has already been holding discussions with powerful Silicon Valley figures about returning as CEO, sources involved in the effort told the Financial Times . An ally of the ex-CEO told the publication that Silicon Valley executives have been putting together a 'war room' to lobby for Huang's return to Nvidia. The executives are hoping to gain backing from the White House , and their efforts are being supported by Huang behind the scenes, the source said. Many investors, Nvidia employees and Silicon Valley executives have also already publicly supported Huang, citing his enormously successful 33-year leadership of the company and vision that placed the business at the heart of the AI boom. President Trump has maintained a positive tone about Huang since the affairs were reported and the ex-CEO stepped down, calling him 'a tremendous talent.' Trump also said, however, that Huang was right to resign if it is confirmed that Alice was a spy. 'It's sad. He’s a tremendous talent. He did something nobody else did. He has a chip that’s so complex, so brilliant, you can’t copy it. What he’s done is incredible, he built an incredible company,' Trump told CNN's Stephen A Smith on Thursday. That could make the ex-CEO's hopes of returning to the company particularly challenging, as 'having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence,' a source involved in the reinstatement efforts admitted to the Financial Times. Huang did not have a controlling share of Nvidia in contrast to many other Silicon Valley executives, which made him unable to override any board decision. The board is now being headed by interim CEO Colette Kress, who previously held the title of Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. extraction.body: Just three days after the high-profile resignation of the founder of the world's most valuable chipmaker, his supporters in Silicon Valley have set up a dedicated war room to pressure the board of directors. However, regaining the seat will not be easy for the billionaire: he does not hold a controlling stake, while the corporation is already scouting for his replacement and bracing for scrutiny from Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Thursday, November 12, following the exposure of extramarital relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct subordinate, is already discussing a plan to return to the company with his confidants. This was reported on Sunday, November 15, by the British newspaper Financial Times. According to an associate of the businessman, Silicon Valley top executives have formed a dedicated "war room" to lobby Nvidia's board of directors for Huang's reinstatement, as well as to try to secure support in the White House. "Everyone who matters in tech outside of the frontier labs loves Jensen," said an interlocutor of the publication, adding that these efforts have the backing of the former CEO himself. Over the weekend, the public campaign for the return of the founder of the $4 trillion corporation gained momentum. An open letter to the board of directors demanding to "Bring Jensen Back" was supported by Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, as well as several Nvidia employees. Back on Friday, major shareholders of the company—Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management head Gavin Baker—published an appeal to the corporate leadership, urging them to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," given his decades of service and the uncertainty surrounding the future of the business. Despite pressure from billionaires and investors, the push to rehabilitate Huang faces severe legal and political obstacles. Unlike many other tech titan founders, Huang does not hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and therefore cannot veto decisions made by the board of directors. The board itself is currently conducting an independent investigation into the former chief's conduct. Even those in the businessman's camp acknowledge the weakness of his position. "An affair with a subordinate is a firing offense," admitted one member of Huang's support group. Aside from the internal workplace affair with Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, Huang's primary problem stems from his connection to Alice Huang, head of the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which US authorities suspect of espionage and smuggling chips into China. This episode has drawn intense scrutiny toward how Nvidia monitors the sales of its artificial intelligence processors to clients in Asia. On Sunday, November 15, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly called for a "radical refresh" in Nvidia's leadership following the departure of its founder. Meanwhile, the corporation's interim CEO Colette Kress is preparing the company for the release of its quarterly financial report on Tuesday, while the board of directors is already looking for a permanent successor. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia representatives have approached Rene Haas, CEO of the British processor architecture designer Arm Holdings, with an offer to head the corporation, though officially the company states that a formal process to select a new leader has not yet been launched. Representatives of Nvidia and Jensen Huang himself declined to comment on his potential return.

extraction.body: An Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset. According to the Times report , which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump. The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year. The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information. The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China. Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. "The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement. Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said. Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China. Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology. As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure. Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China. Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers. The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed. "Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. extraction.body: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. passages: [BEIJING] Nvidia has said US export controls have effectively shut it out of China’s artificial intelligence data centre market, but a Reuters review has identified more than US$3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around the American chipmaker’s restricted processors.

The findings come a day after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive amid a scandal over his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of intelligence ties to Beijing .
Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation , saying it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security were compromised.
There has been no public finding that Jensen Huang violated export-control laws.
But an IDC report cited by Reuters in October estimated Nvidia still accounted for 34 per cent of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in the first half of 2026.
Jensen Huang discusses comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies: report
Huang, a vocal advocate of easing export restrictions, said in 2025 Nvidia’s market share in China had fallen from 95 per cent to zero.

The projects, stretching from China’s wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing’s access to the technology powering the global AI boom .
The estimate includes planned investments and signed contracts as well as completed installations.
It covers buildings, power systems and other infrastructure, and does not reflect spending on Nvidia chips alone.
Huang’s departure could deepen these vulnerabilities by weakening Nvidia’s lobbying leverage as US lawmakers press for tighter controls.

The scrutiny has intensified since Huang’s resignation on Thursday (Nov 12), following allegations involving Alice Huang, a former executive associated with Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner Megaspeed .

sources.title: How Asian governments responded to NVIDIA CEO's departure
passages: Jensen Huang's departure from NVIDIA has sparked varied reactions across Asia, with some governments confirming their commitment to chip supplies and others assessing the impact on local projects or ongoing investigations.
Taipei's city government also confirmed that NVIDIA's planned overseas headquarters in Taipei remains on track despite this leadership change.
However, Huang's exit has raised concerns over more than $3 billion worth of Chinese AI computing projects dependent on NVIDIA's restricted processors.
The ministry also opposed export controls disrupting global supply chains and denied knowledge of reports connecting restricted NVIDIA chips with a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang.
Japan's Industry Ministry has said it will closely monitor NVIDIA after Huang's resignation, considering the chipmaker a key player in Japan's AI semiconductor industry.

extraction.body: Jensen Huang's departure from NVIDIA has sparked varied reactions across Asia, with some governments confirming their commitment to chip supplies and others assessing the impact on local projects or ongoing investigations. The move comes after reports of a Chinese spy operation targeting Huang and his admission of an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. China's foreign ministry has denied allegations that a Chinese businesswoman linked to Huang was a spy, calling them baseless and an attempt to defame Beijing. The ministry also opposed export controls disrupting global supply chains and denied knowledge of reports connecting restricted NVIDIA chips with a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang. However, Huang's exit has raised concerns over more than $3 billion worth of Chinese AI computing projects dependent on NVIDIA's restricted processors. In Singapore, authorities seized Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed's passport in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases. The probe looked into whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. While police found insufficient evidence to prove offenses related to false declarations in February 2026, they said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. South Korea's Science Ministry said NVIDIA had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Meanwhile, Taiwan's Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang's departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry. Taipei's city government also confirmed that NVIDIA's planned overseas headquarters in Taipei remains on track despite this leadership change. Japan's Industry Ministry has said it will closely monitor NVIDIA after Huang's resignation, considering the chipmaker a key player in Japan's AI semiconductor industry. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it's too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry but emphasized Japan's commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors.

coreStoryFacts.text: Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump.

The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.
Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports.
H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.
Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.
Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls.
The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information.
Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China.

Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects.

extraction.body: An Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset. According to the Times report , which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump. The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year. The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information. The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China. Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. "The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement. Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said. Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China. Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology. As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure. Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China. Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers. The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed. "Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. extraction.body: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. Taipei's city government also confirmed that NVIDIA's planned overseas headquarters in Taipei remains on track despite this leadership change.

extraction.body: Jensen Huang's departure from NVIDIA has sparked varied reactions across Asia, with some governments confirming their commitment to chip supplies and others assessing the impact on local projects or ongoing investigations. The move comes after reports of a Chinese spy operation targeting Huang and his admission of an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. China's foreign ministry has denied allegations that a Chinese businesswoman linked to Huang was a spy, calling them baseless and an attempt to defame Beijing. The ministry also opposed export controls disrupting global supply chains and denied knowledge of reports connecting restricted NVIDIA chips with a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang. However, Huang's exit has raised concerns over more than $3 billion worth of Chinese AI computing projects dependent on NVIDIA's restricted processors. In Singapore, authorities seized Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed's passport in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases. The probe looked into whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. While police found insufficient evidence to prove offenses related to false declarations in February 2026, they said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. South Korea's Science Ministry said NVIDIA had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Meanwhile, Taiwan's Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang's departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry. Taipei's city government also confirmed that NVIDIA's planned overseas headquarters in Taipei remains on track despite this leadership change. Japan's Industry Ministry has said it will closely monitor NVIDIA after Huang's resignation, considering the chipmaker a key player in Japan's AI semiconductor industry. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it's too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry but emphasized Japan's commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors.

extraction.body: We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.” “Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.” Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem. Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here . Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days. Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned. But someone said to me, “If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. I mean, no one is quite as special as Elon is, but it’s a big, incredibly successful company. Like you said — in a lot of ways, the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia. And for most people, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. He’s the biggest shareholder. He has family members who work at the company, and probably most importantly, there was no succession plan in place. So this was not something that they were prepared for at all. Rebecca: I think we should actually take a step back, because we just launched into this conversation assuming — rightly so — that our listeners will know what the heck we’re talking about. But for those who somehow don’t, Jensen resigned on Thursday, after it came out he was having an affair with a former executive at an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, who’s alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. And then there was another reported affair with an Nvidia executive. So he’s resigned. Nvidia CFO Collette Kress is jumping in as the interim CEO. She’s a longtime board member. I think it’s always interesting when a CFO steps in to be a CEO. It just means we’re going to manage expenses right now, like that’s the key. Anthony: I think a big part of the message is: This is not necessarily someone you should expect to be in this role for the long term. No disrespect to her, but it feels like a caretaker appointment while they figure things out. Just to get into that backstory a little bit more, what has been really remarkable to me has been this sense that a lot of what ultimately brought Huang down, [that] stuff was at least known in intelligence circles for a while. Apparently, this report that [raises] questions, concerns about his relationship with Alice Huang is something that was circulating a year ago, or close to a year ago. And then suddenly, everything really accelerated, Starting over the weekend, with Jensen Huang admitting to having an affair, the board saying it was investigating, but that it still had a lot of faith in him. And then this week, this other affair being reported on, and it just felt like there was all this bad news coming fairly quickly. But also, it wasn’t this thing that no one had known before. I guess a lot of the general public hadn’t known. So it’s this combined feeling of, “Wow, the ground kind of shifted so quickly under him,” even though the worst stuff, the possibility that somehow national security might have been threatened, is something that actually has been known by the government for nearly a year, if not more. Rebecca: That’s exactly right. Trump was given some warnings about Huang’s affair with someone who has ties to Chinese intelligence, potentially, and it seemed like he didn’t really mind. I think what’s important here, though, is to note that Jensen Huang has been an advocate for loosening chip exports to China. And so this is where the crux of it is. Can anyone trust him as the CEO of this company when he’s advocating for loosening chip exports to China? Which a lot of people believe is a national security issue, because that means it will give Chinese AI companies access to our powerful chips, which will help them improve their AI, which could threaten America. I mean, there’s two sides of this coin. And I think, honestly, that Jensen does not need a woman to tell him that — he just wants to sell more chips, and to anybody and everybody, and whether or not that’s good for national security or not, I think is honestly secondary to him. Tim: I completely agree. I think the big turning point seems to happen on November 9 — so that would have been earlier this week, Monday, when the Bloomberg report came out and suggested that Nvidia’s head attorney had some role in inquiring about the Department of Commerce’s investigation into Alice Huang. Things seem to have accelerated in the last few days following that. And I don’t know what role exactly that report played in it, but it seems to be maybe there was a shift within government or within the board, a kind of a daunting realization of the extent to which this had spread just beyond Jensen and some affair. Anthony: There’s also just the question of: What does this mean for Nvidia? What does this mean for the broader AI industry? And one of the reasons those two things are very tightly connected is not just Nvidia chips themselves, but also the fact that under Jensen Huang, the company has invested very, very heavily in a number of AI startups. People talk about the idea of an AI circular economy, and I think Nvidia has been one of the biggest players in that, in terms of both funding a lot of things, [but] also, obviously, providing the infrastructure for a lot of AI projects. So if Nvidia is going into this stage of lockdown, circle the wagons — even if it just means a small pullback, that could have really dramatic repercussions. Rebecca: Yeah, that’s what I want to know: What happens to the Bank of Nvidia without Jensen? Is he the one leading this? Just to throw some numbers at you, Nvidia apparently accounts for roughly 80% of the AI GPU market. It reported $99 billion in investments and another $25 billion in commitments, plus $36 billion dollars in cloud service commitments. A lot of those include investments into CoreWeave, Nebius, OpenAI, Anthropic, major data center projects. They’ve got their fingers in literally everybody’s pie. Where was Nvidia’s security team?
